hot.title: Qwen3.5-Omni Technical Report
hot.summary: The Qwen Team introduced Qwen3.5-Omni, a fully omnimodal Large Language Model capable of understanding, reasoning, and generating content across text, images, audio, and video modalities. This model achieved state-of-the-art performance across 215 audio and audio-visual benchmarks, demonstrated enhanced real-time interaction with low latency, and exhibited emergent capabilities like "Audio-Visual Vibe Coding."

hot.title: Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence
hot.summary: Renmin University of China and ByteDance Seed researchers introduced Agent-World, a framework for advancing general agent intelligence through scalable real-world environment synthesis and a continuous self-evolving training mechanism. The approach enables agents to learn and adapt by autonomously discovering and constructing a diverse ecosystem of stateful, executable tools and environments from real-world sources, achieving consistent performance improvements across 23 challenging agent benchmarks and outperforming prior environment-scaling methods.

hot.title: OneVL: One-Step Latent Reasoning and Planning with Vision-Language Explanation
hot.summary: The Xiaomi Embodied Intelligence Team developed OneVL, a framework integrating a Vision-Language-Action model with a world model auxiliary for autonomous driving, which is the first latent Chain-of-Thought (CoT) method to surpass explicit autoregressive CoT in trajectory prediction performance while maintaining answer-only inference latency. OneVL achieved an 88.84 PDM-score on NAVSIM, outperforming prior 8B models by up to 2.64 points, with inference latency comparable to answer-only prediction.

hot.title: Learning Whole-Body Humanoid Locomotion via Motion Generation and Motion Tracking
hot.summary: This research introduces a whole-body humanoid locomotion framework that merges a diffusion-based motion generator with an RL-based motion tracker. The system enables the Unitree G1 robot to adaptively navigate diverse, challenging terrains in real-time by producing perception-aware reference motions and executing them robustly.

hot.title: MultiWorld: Scalable Multi-Agent Multi-View Video World Models
hot.summary: MultiWorld presents a framework for scalable multi-agent, multi-view video world modeling, integrating a Multi-Agent Condition Module (MACM) and a Global State Encoder (GSE). The model demonstrates improved action controllability, multi-view consistency, and scalability across varying numbers of agents and camera views, outperforming baselines on multi-player game and multi-robot manipulation tasks.

hot.title: Do Vision-Language Models Truly Perform Vision Reasoning? A Rigorous Study of the Modality Gap
hot.summary: Researchers at Nanyang Technological University introduce CROSSMATH, a novel multimodal reasoning benchmark designed to rigorously assess whether Vision-Language Models (VLMs) truly perform visual reasoning or primarily rely on text. The study reveals a substantial performance gap in VLMs when reasoning with images versus text, but demonstrates that targeted post-training strategies can significantly enhance visual reasoning capabilities and improve out-of-domain generalization, such as increasing Qwen3.5-9B's image-only Macro Accuracy from 3.2% to 50.4%.

hot.title: LLM Reasoning Is Latent, Not the Chain of Thought
hot.summary: Research demonstrates that the core mechanism of Large Language Model reasoning is primarily driven by internal latent-state trajectories, rather than solely by explicit chains of thought, with the dominant factor shifting based on the task's structural demands. This work provides a framework to differentiate and empirically validate how generic computation, surface verbalizations, or latent dynamics mediate performance gains in LLMs.

hot.title: (1D) Ordered Tokens Enable Efficient Test-Time Search
hot.summary: This research reveals that 1D ordered tokenization, which processes images from coarse-to-fine semantic detail, intrinsically improves the efficiency of test-time search in autoregressive image generation models. This enables more effective zero-shot multimodal control and even training-free generation, outperforming traditional 2D grid tokenization in inference-time scaling.

hot.title: Fisher Decorator: Refining Flow Policy via A Local Transport Map
hot.summary: The Fisher Decorator (FiDec) framework refines flow-based offline reinforcement learning policies using a local transport map and Fisher information matrix-based regularization. This approach enables geometry-aware, anisotropic policy updates, achieving state-of-the-art performance across OGBench and D4RL benchmarks while mitigating mode collapse and distributional shift.

hot.title: EasyVideoR1: Easier RL for Video Understanding
hot.summary: EasyVideoR1 introduces a comprehensive reinforcement learning framework for large vision-language models, specifically designed for video understanding. It achieved a 1.47x throughput improvement in RL training and enhanced the average accuracy of a Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct model by +2.3 points across 10 video benchmarks, including a +6.6% gain on Video-Holmes and +6.7% on VideoMathQA.

hot.title: When Can LLMs Learn to Reason with Weak Supervision?
hot.summary: An investigation systematically characterizes the conditions under which large language models (LLMs) generalize with Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) under weak supervision. The study reveals that effective learning relies on prolonged training reward pre-saturation and faithful reasoning, which is significantly enhanced by supervised fine-tuning on explicit reasoning traces.

hot.title: Neural Garbage Collection: Learning to Forget while Learning to Reason
hot.summary: Researchers at Stanford University developed Neural Garbage Collection (NGC), an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework that allows large language models to jointly learn chain-of-thought reasoning and KV cache memory management. This method effectively reduces peak KV cache size by 2.4x to 5x while consistently outperforming heuristic eviction strategies across various arithmetic and mathematical reasoning tasks.

hot.title: SkillFlow:Benchmarking Lifelong Skill Discovery and Evolution for Autonomous Agents
hot.summary: SKILLFLOW, a new benchmark, evaluates how autonomous agents continuously discover, repair, and manage skills from their own experience across sequential tasks. Experiments reveal that leading LLM-based agents exhibit varied capacities for skill evolution, with some improving task success by over 8% through effective skill refinement, while others struggle with skill fragmentation and propagating errors.

hot.title: Dive into Claude Code: The Design Space of Today's and Future AI Agent Systems
hot.summary: A detailed architectural analysis of Anthropic's Claude Code, a production-grade AI agent, is provided through source-level examination, revealing a design philosophy prioritizing a robust operational harness over raw AI decision logic. The study contrasts this with OpenClaw, an open-source system, to highlight how different deployment contexts influence architectural choices and identifies future design challenges for agent systems.

hot.title: π0.7π_{0.7}π0.7​: a Steerable Generalist Robotic Foundation Model with Emergent Capabilities
hot.summary: Researchers at Physical Intelligence developed π0.7, a 5-billion-parameter generalist robotic foundation model. This model utilizes a diversified prompting strategy, incorporating language instructions, episode metadata, and generated subgoal images, to achieve strong out-of-the-box performance and compositional generalization across diverse tasks and robot platforms.

hot.title: Prefill-as-a-Service: KVCache of Next-Generation Models Could Go Cross-Datacenter
hot.summary: The Prefill-as-a-Service (PrfaaS) architecture from Moonshot AI and Tsinghua University enables practical cross-datacenter prefill-decode disaggregation for hybrid-attention large language models by transferring KVCache over commodity Ethernet. This system achieves 54% higher throughput and a 50% reduction in mean Time-To-First-Token compared to a homogeneous baseline, utilizing only 13% of available inter-cluster bandwidth.

hot.title: Geometric Context Transformer for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
hot.summary: LingBot-Map, a feed-forward 3D foundation model, performs streaming 3D reconstruction by introducing a Geometric Context Transformer (GCT) that employs a novel attention mechanism to manage multi-level geometric context. The system achieves superior accuracy and efficiency in camera pose estimation and dense 3D reconstruction compared to existing streaming methods, operating at approximately 20 FPS for sequences up to 10,000 frames.

hot.title: ClawEnvKit: Automatic Environment Generation for Claw-Like Agents
hot.summary: ClawEnvKit introduces a framework for automatically generating diverse, verified environments for "claw-like" large language model agents, enabling on-demand creation of evaluation and training tasks from natural language specifications. The system significantly reduces environment construction costs by up to 13,800x compared to manual curation, while achieving or exceeding the quality of human-curated benchmarks.

hot.title: OpenGame: Open Agentic Coding for Games
hot.summary: OpenGame is an open-source agentic framework that autonomously generates fully playable 2D web games from natural language specifications. It leverages a domain-specialized code model, a structured multimodal coding agent, and "Game Skill" to achieve 72.4 Build Health, 67.2 Visual Usability, and 65.1 Intent Alignment on a custom benchmark, surpassing prior methods.

hot.title: Extending One-Step Image Generation from Class Labels to Text via Discriminative Text Representation
hot.summary: Researchers from Nankai University and Alibaba Group successfully extended MeanFlow's efficient one-step image generation from class labels to text inputs by developing a framework that leverages text representations with high discriminability and disentanglement. This approach achieves comparable image quality to multi-step baselines (e.g., 0.90 GenEval score at 4 steps vs. 0.91 at 30 steps for BLIP3o-NEXT) while significantly accelerating inference time.

likes.title: Perception Encoder: The best visual embeddings are not at the output of  the network
likes.summary: Perception Encoder introduces a family of vision models that achieve state-of-the-art performance across diverse vision and vision-language tasks, demonstrating that general, high-quality visual features can be extracted from the intermediate layers of a single, contrastively-trained network. It provides specific alignment tuning methods to make these features accessible for tasks ranging from zero-shot classification to dense spatial prediction and multimodal language understanding.

likes.title: TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TTRL is a framework enabling Large Language Models to self-improve through Reinforcement Learning on unlabeled test data, using self-generated rewards derived from majority voting. This approach substantially boosts performance on complex reasoning tasks, with one model achieving a 211% improvement on AIME 2024, by fostering a self-reinforcing learning loop.

likes.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI and Tsinghua University developed Self-Principled Critique Tuning (SPCT) and DeepSeek-GRM models, a pointwise generative reward modeling approach that achieves state-of-the-art performance in generalist reward benchmarks. This method demonstrates effective inference-time scalability, allowing smaller models to match or exceed the performance of much larger models by leveraging increased compute during inference, thereby improving LLM alignment.

likes.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
likes.summary: Research from Tsinghua University reveals that current Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) primarily enhances the sampling efficiency of Large Language Models for already existing reasoning patterns. This optimization often narrows the models' overall reasoning capacity at higher pass@k values, contrasting with distillation, which effectively expands their problem-solving scope.

likes.title: Reasoning Models Can Be Effective Without Thinking
likes.summary: Ma et al. demonstrated that Large Language Models trained for Chain-of-Thought reasoning can achieve comparable or superior performance without generating explicit reasoning steps, utilizing a technique called 'NoThinking'. This approach significantly reduces inference latency by up to 9x and token usage by up to 5.1x, particularly when combined with parallel sampling, offering a more efficient paradigm for LLM reasoning.

likes.title: Synthetic Data Generation & Multi-Step RL for Reasoning & Tool Use
likes.summary: SWiRL is an offline multi-step reinforcement learning methodology designed to enhance Large Language Models' reasoning and tool-use capabilities. It generates and utilizes synthetic data, applying process-based filtering for step-wise optimization, which leads to substantial performance gains and strong cross-domain generalization in complex tasks.

likes.title: ReTool: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs
likes.summary: ReTool, developed by ByteDance Seed, introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enables Large Language Models to strategically use code interpreters for complex problem-solving. It achieved 67.0% accuracy on the AIME 2024 benchmark, significantly improving performance over text-based reasoning and demonstrating emergent self-correction capabilities in code generation.

likes.title: Hogwild! Inference: Parallel LLM Generation via Concurrent Attention
likes.summary: Researchers from Yandex, HSE University, and IST Austria developed "Hogwild! Inference," a protocol enabling multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate text concurrently by sharing a dynamically updated attention Key-Value (KV) cache. This mechanism allows LLMs to self-organize and collaborate in real-time, achieving up to 3.6x speedup and improved accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.

likes.title: Challenges and Paths Towards AI for Software Engineering
likes.summary: This paper presents a strategic roadmap for the field of AI in software engineering, providing a comprehensive taxonomy of software development tasks and identifying nine key bottlenecks that impede current AI capabilities. It proposes a targeted set of research directions focused on data collection, training, and inference-time approaches to advance automated software development.

likes.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
likes.summary: Researchers from ByteDance Seed, Tsinghua University, and The University of Hong Kong developed DAPO, an open-source reinforcement learning system for large language models. The system achieved 50 points on the AIME 2024 dataset with a Qwen2.5-32B model, surpassing the prior 47-point score of DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B while requiring 50% fewer training steps.

likes.title: Proof or Bluff? Evaluating LLMs on 2025 USA Math Olympiad
likes.summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and INSAIT conducted the first evaluation of large language models on generating rigorous natural language proofs for problems from the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. The study found that most state-of-the-art models scored below 5% of the maximum points, with the highest-performing model, GEMINI-2.5-PRO, achieving only 24.4%, demonstrating fundamental shortcomings in advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities.

likes.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI developed DeepSeek-R1, an LLM demonstrating that sophisticated reasoning capabilities can emerge through pure outcome-based reinforcement learning without reliance on human-annotated reasoning trajectories. The model achieved an AIME 2024 pass@1 accuracy of 77.9% with R1-Zero, and the multi-stage DeepSeek-R1 surpassed state-of-the-art models on numerous math, coding, and STEM benchmarks while exhibiting emergent self-reflection and dynamic strategy adaptation.

likes.title: ReSearch: Learning to Reason with Search for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The ReSearch framework enables Large Language Models to integrate multi-step reasoning with external search, learning interactively via reinforcement learning without supervised intermediate steps. It yields substantial performance gains on complex multi-hop question answering benchmarks and reveals emergent self-correction capabilities.

likes.title: Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures
likes.summary: DeepSeek-V3 showcases how a hardware-software co-design strategy can achieve state-of-the-art large language model performance using a comparatively modest cluster of 2,048 NVIDIA H800 GPUs. The paper highlights innovations like Multi-head Latent Attention, DeepSeekMoE, FP8 mixed-precision training, and a Multi-Plane Fat-Tree network, which collectively reduce memory consumption, lower training costs, and accelerate inference.

likes.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
likes.summary: Researchers from NVIDIA and leading universities introduce Test-Time Training (TTT) layers within pre-trained Diffusion Transformers to generate one-minute-long videos from text storyboards, enabling coherent multi-scene narratives while addressing the computational limitations of traditional self-attention mechanisms for long sequences.

likes.title: Sequential Task Assignment and Resource Allocation in V2X-Enabled Mobile  Edge Computing
likes.summary: A multi-tier task offloading mechanism for V2X-enabled Mobile Edge Computing efficiently processes sequential subtasks from vehicular applications by first leveraging proximate vehicle resources and then RSU-based MEC. The system minimizes energy consumption while meeting stringent delay requirements through joint optimization of offloading decisions, communication, and computation resource allocation, demonstrating superior performance over various baselines.

likes.title: How new data permeates LLM knowledge and how to dilute it
likes.summary: Research from Google DeepMind reveals how new knowledge permeates through large language models, demonstrating that surprising information (measured by token probability) leads to broader changes across model behavior, while introducing "stepping-stone" text augmentation and "ignore-k" update pruning techniques that reduce undesirable priming effects by 50-95%.

likes.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
likes.summary: Titans introduces a new neural memory module that learns to memorize information at test time and effectively combines with attention mechanisms for better long-term sequence modeling

likes.title: PHYBench: Holistic Evaluation of Physical Perception and Reasoning in  Large Language Models
likes.summary: PHYBench, a new benchmark developed by the School of Physics at Peking University, rigorously evaluates large language models' physical perception and reasoning using 500 original, human-curated physics problems. Evaluations revealed a substantial performance gap between LLMs and human experts, with the best LLM achieving 36.9% accuracy compared to the human baseline of 61.9%.

likes.title: Transformers without Normalization
likes.summary: This research introduces Dynamic Tanh (DyT), a simple element-wise function designed as a drop-in replacement for normalization layers in Transformers. Models equipped with DyT achieve performance comparable to or exceeding their normalized counterparts across a wide range of tasks including computer vision, large language models, and speech processing, often without requiring extensive hyperparameter tuning.
